name: scam_en_10_gov_official
key_sentence: To prove your innocence, we need to check your funds. Transfer your savings into a safety account that we provide.
why: Bank claim (1) and police claim (7) give impersonation; threat of arrest (8) gives urgency. Line 11 asks to move savings to a 'safety account': money + another signal already up -> red.

name: scam_en_11_bank_otp
key_sentence: I am sending a six-digit code to your phone now. Please read it out to me.
why: Bank claim (1) and 'act immediately' (7) are in place; line 9 asks the victim to read out the code sent to their phone.

name: scam_en_12_parcel_customs
key_sentence: You need to pay a release fee of four hundred and eighty dollars through PayNow.
why: Courier + customs officer claims (1, 6) and threat of police referral (8); line 10 demands a PayNow release fee.

name: scam_en_13_tech_support
key_sentence: Yes, we must move your money to a protected account before the hackers take it. Please do it right now.
why: Provider claim (1); remote-access code request (9) and 'log in to your banking' (11) build up; line 13 says to move money to a protected account 'right now'.

name: scam_en_14_friend_in_trouble
key_sentence: Can you PayNow it now? I'll give you the number. It's really urgent, they are waiting.
why: Fake relative (1-3), police/bail story (5, 7); line 9-10 gives the amount and asks for an urgent PayNow.

name: scam_zh_10_gov_official
key_sentence: 为了证明您的清白，我们需要核查您的资金，请把您的存款转到我们提供的安全账户。
why: Bank claim (1) and police claim (7) give impersonation; threat of arrest (8) gives urgency. Line 11 asks to move savings to a 'safety account': money + another signal already up -> red.

name: scam_zh_12_parcel_customs
key_sentence: 您需要通过PayNow缴付四百八十元的放行费。
why: Courier + customs officer claims (1, 6) and threat of police referral (8); line 10 demands a PayNow release fee.

name: normal_en_10_bank_reminder
why: Hard negative: a real bank mentions an amount, a due date and says it will never ask for your OTP. Should not turn red.

name: normal_en_11_clinic_appointment
why: Appointment details and a consultation fee at the counter. No pressure, no payment request over the phone.

name: normal_en_12_delivery_driver
why: Hard negative: driver states a price and offers cash or PayNow at the door. Should not turn red.

name: normal_en_13_insurance_sales
why: Hard negative: sales call with a premium and a mild 'promotion ends this month'. Yellow is acceptable, red is a false alarm.

name: normal_en_14_family_call
why: Hard negative: 'I'll PayNow you back' in a family chat. Should not turn red.

name: normal_zh_10_bank_reminder
why: Hard negative: a real bank mentions an amount, a due date and says it will never ask for your OTP. Should not turn red.

name: normal_zh_14_family_call
why: Hard negative: 'I'll PayNow you back' in a family chat. Should not turn red.

name: scam_en_20_ica_to_china_police
scam_type: ICA officer -> fake China police (SPF advisories Aug/Sep 2026)
key_sentence: To clear your name, you must move all your savings into a supervision account so we can check the money is clean.
why: ICA claim (1) and 'your passport was used' (3) give impersonation; the transfer to a Chinese police officer (7) and the threat of arrest (9) add urgency. Line 11 asks for the savings to be moved into a 'supervision account': money + impersonation -> red.
added: 2026-11, from SPF's 2026 scam advisories (dialogue written by the team)

name: scam_en_21_telco_to_mas_officer
scam_type: telco staff -> fake MAS officer, number starting with 3 (SPF advisory Jul 2026)
key_sentence: To protect it, transfer your balance to a MAS safety account now. You will get it back after the investigation.
why: Red from line 5 is fine: that is where the call is handed to a fake official. Telco claim (1) and a hand-off to a 'Monetary Authority' officer (5) give impersonation; 'frozen within the hour' (7) gives urgency. Line 9 asks to transfer the balance to a MAS 'safety account': money + other signals -> red.
added: 2026-11, from SPF's 2026 scam advisories (dialogue written by the team)

name: scam_en_22_apple_support_crypto
scam_type: Apple support impersonation, crypto account takeover (SPF advisory Aug 2026)
key_sentence: Transfer all your coins to the Apple secure wallet address I'm sending you, then read me the six-digit code you receive.
why: Apple claim (1) gives impersonation; 'someone is logging in right now' (3) gives urgency. Line 9 asks to move the crypto to a 'secure wallet' and read out the code: money -> red.
added: 2026-11, from SPF's 2026 scam advisories (dialogue written by the team)

name: scam_en_23_bank_card_handover
scam_type: bank staff, hand over card and PIN / ATM transfer (SPF advisory May 2026)
key_sentence: Put the card in an envelope and write your PIN on a note inside, so we can cancel it properly.
why: Red from line 5 is fine: telling the victim to avoid the branch is a scam sign on its own. Bank claim (1) gives impersonation; 'compromised, act today' (3) gives urgency. Line 9 asks for the card and PIN to be handed to a courier: money + other signals -> red.
added: 2026-11, from SPF's 2026 scam advisories (dialogue written by the team)

name: scam_en_24_job_task_deposit
scam_type: job / task scam (top 3 by cases, SPF Annual Scam Brief 2025)
key_sentence: You top up five hundred dollars to the merchant account, and you get it back with thirty percent commission.
why: A recruiter (not an official) gives little impersonation; the money ask is the signal. Line 9 asks for a deposit to 'unlock' the commission, with a deadline: money + urgency -> red.
known_result: Measured 2026-11-13: stays UNSURE (never red). No one is impersonated, so the current models miss it: a good scam to teach through the learning loop (report it, label it, retrain).
added: 2026-11, from SPF's 2026 scam advisories (dialogue written by the team)

name: scam_zh_20_ica_to_china_police
scam_type: ICA officer -> fake China police, Mandarin (SPF advisory Aug 2026)
key_sentence: 为了证明您的清白，请马上把银行里的存款全部转到我们指定的安全账户。
why: ICA claim (1) and the Chinese police hand-off (5) give impersonation; arrest threat (7) gives urgency. Line 9 asks to transfer the savings to a 'safe account'.
added: 2026-11, from SPF's 2026 scam advisories (dialogue written by the team)

name: normal_en_20_ica_passport_collection
why: Hard negative for the ICA scam: a real ICA reminder names the agency and the passport but asks for nothing, sends the person to the official app and says ICA never asks for money by phone. Should not turn red.
added: 2026-11, from SPF's 2026 scam advisories (dialogue written by the team)

name: normal_en_21_bank_fraud_check
why: Hard negative for the bank card scam: a real fraud team asks only yes/no about one transaction, blocks the card itself and tells the customer to call back on the number on the card. 'Fraud', 'card' and 'block' appear, but no money or code is asked for.
known_result: Measured 2026-11-13: FALSE ALARM, red at line 5 (bank + fraud + card words). A real false alarm to send back with "This was fine".
added: 2026-11, from SPF's 2026 scam advisories (dialogue written by the team)

name: normal_en_22_telco_contract_renewal
why: Hard negative for the telco scam: a real telco sales call about a contract ending, with a price and a 'limited time' offer, but no transfer to any official and nothing to pay on the call.
added: 2026-11, from SPF's 2026 scam advisories (dialogue written by the team)
